expectedText:
FARM LABOR CONTRACTOR LICENSING — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS FARM LABOR CONTRACTOR LICENSING INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Farm Labor Contractor Licensing Law, Labor Code Sections 1682 through 1699, which requires a person who recruits, supplies, or hires workers for a fee on behalf of an agricultural employer -- and who furnishes board, lodging, or transportation, supervises or directs the work, or disburses wages in connection with that activity -- to hold a license issued by the Labor Commissioner before acting as a farm labor contractor. Acme, Inc. has described its use of labor contractors, if any, as follows: We use a staffing agency to supply approximately 20 warehouse workers. This document states the content of the statute; it does not determine whether any particular individual or arrangement meets the statutory definition of "farm labor contractor," and it is not a substitute for individualized legal advice or for consulting a licensed attorney.

WHO IS A "FARM LABOR CONTRACTOR" UNDER LABOR CODE SECTION 1682
Labor Code Section 1682 defines a "farm labor contractor" as any person who, for a fee, employs workers to render personal services in connection with the production of farm products to, for, or under the direction of a third person, or who recruits, solicits, supplies, or hires workers on behalf of an agricultural employer, and who -- for that fee -- also furnishes board, lodging, or transportation for the workers, supervises or otherwise directs or measures their work, or disburses wage payments to them. Section 1682.5 removes two categories of activity from the chapter's coverage entirely: services performed by a nonprofit corporation or organization for its own members, and services performed by a person only within the scope of that person's employment by the third person on whose behalf the person is acting, provided the person is not acting as an independent contractor.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Farm labor contractor” designates any person who, for a fee, employs workers to render personal services in connection with the production of any farm products to, for, or under the direction of a third person, or who recruits, solicits, supplies, or hires workers on behalf of an employer engaged in the growing or producing of farm products, and who, for a fee, provides in connection therewith one or more of the following services: furnishes board, lodging, or transportation for those workers; supervises, times, checks, counts, weighs, or otherwise directs or measures their work; or disburses wage payments to these persons."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1682(b) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, definition of "farm labor contractor" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1682.)
  "A nonprofit corporation or organization with respect to services specified in subdivision (b) of Section 1682, which are performed for its members."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1682.5(a) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, nonprofit-member-services exemption (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1682.5.)
  "Any person who performs the services specified in subdivision (b) of Section 1682 only within the scope of his employment by the third person on whose behalf he is so acting and not as an independent contractor."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1682.5(b) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, employee-acting-within-scope-of-employment exemption (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1682.5.)
  Known gap: The statute's exemptions turn on whether a person is acting "within the scope of his employment" for the user of the labor rather than as an independent contractor, and on whether an organization is a genuine "nonprofit corporation or organization" acting "for its members"; Section 1682.5 does not itself define those terms or state how they interact with the multi-factor tests used elsewhere in California law (such as the ABC test) to distinguish employees from independent contractors, so this sheet does not resolve how the exemption applies to any particular arrangement.

LICENSE REQUIREMENT AND CIVIL PENALTY FOR ACTING WITHOUT ONE
Labor Code Section 1683(a) states that a person shall not act as a farm labor contractor until a license has been issued by the Labor Commissioner and the license is in full force and effect and in the person's possession. Subdivision (b) establishes a tiered civil penalty schedule for a violation of this licensing requirement: an initial citation carries a penalty of $100 per farmworker employed by the unlicensed person plus $100 per calendar day of violation, capped at $10,000; a second citation doubles those figures to $200 per farmworker and per day, capped at $20,000; and a third or subsequent citation raises the figures to $500 per farmworker and per day, capped at $50,000.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A person shall not act as a farm labor contractor until a license to do so has been issued to the person by the Labor Commissioner and the license is in full force and effect and in the person’s possession."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1683(a) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, license required to act as a farm labor contractor (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1683.)
  "For any initial citation, one hundred dollars ($100) for each farmworker employed by the unlicensed person, plus one hundred dollars ($100) for each calendar day that a violation occurs, for a total penalty not to exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000)."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1683(b)(1)(A) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, initial-citation civil penalty tier (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1683.)
  Known gap: Section 1683's civil penalty schedule applies to the act of operating without a license; it does not by its own text address the separate question of whether, or under what circumstances, an agricultural employer who engages an unlicensed farm labor contractor (as opposed to the contractor itself) bears civil liability, which may instead arise under other statutes such as Labor Code Section 2810.3 or general joint-employer principles that are outside this chapter and not addressed by this sheet.

LICENSE APPLICATION: SWORN STATEMENT AND COMMISSIONER INVESTIGATION
Under Labor Code Section 1684(a), the Labor Commissioner may not issue or renew a farm labor contractor license until several conditions are satisfied. Among them, the applicant must execute a written application, subscribed and sworn to, in a form prescribed by the Labor Commissioner, that discloses the applicant's character, competency, and responsibility, the names and addresses of anyone else financially interested in the proposed operation, a consent to service of process on the Labor Commissioner if the applicant later becomes unavailable for service, and the names of persons who performed farm-labor-contracting services on the applicant's behalf in the preceding calendar year. The Labor Commissioner must also independently investigate and become satisfied as to the applicant's character, competency, and responsibility before a license may issue.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The person has executed a written application in a form prescribed by the Labor Commissioner, subscribed and sworn to by the person, and containing all of the following:"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, written and sworn license application requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  "The Labor Commissioner, after investigation, is satisfied as to the character, competency, and responsibility of the person."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, Labor Commissioner investigation requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  Known gap: This clause describes only the sworn-application and character-investigation conditions in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subdivision (a); it does not restate the bond, fee, examination, sexual harassment training, or federal registration conditions that appear in the remaining paragraphs of the same subdivision (addressed in separate clauses of this sheet), and the statute does not itself specify the evidentiary standard or procedure the Labor Commissioner uses to become "satisfied" as to character, competency, and responsibility.

SURETY BOND AND LICENSE FEE TIED TO PAYROLL SIZE
Labor Code Section 1684(a)(3) requires an applicant to deposit a surety bond with the Labor Commissioner in an amount tied to the size of the applicant's annual payroll: a $25,000 bond for payrolls up to $500,000, a $50,000 bond for payrolls between $500,000 and $2,000,000, and a $75,000 bond for payrolls above $2,000,000. Subdivision (a)(4) requires payment of a license fee, stated in the current text as $500 plus a $10 filing fee (not required on a timely renewal application), with the license fee itself having increased by $100 to $600 effective January 1, 2015. A portion of each licensee's annual fee -- $150, as stated in the current text -- is deposited into the Farmworker Remedial Account, from which the Labor Commissioner disburses funds to persons determined to have been damaged by a licensed or unlicensed farm labor contractor.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The person has deposited with the Labor Commissioner a surety bond in an amount based on the size of the person’s annual payroll for all employees, as follows: (i) For payrolls up to five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000), a twenty-five-thousand-dollar ($25,000) bond. (ii) For payrolls of five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) to two million dollars ($2,000,000), a fifty-thousand-dollar ($50,000) bond. (iii) For payrolls greater than two million dollars ($2,000,000), a seventy-five-thousand-dollar ($75,000) bond."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(3)(A) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, payroll-tiered surety bond amounts (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  "The person has paid to the Labor Commissioner a license fee of five hundred dollars ($500) plus a filing fee of ten dollars ($10). However, when a timely application for renewal is filed, the ten-dollar ($10) filing fee is not required. The license fee shall increase by one hundred dollars ($100), to six hundred dollars ($600), on January 1, 2015."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(4) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, license fee and filing fee (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  "The Labor Commissioner shall deposit one hundred fifty dollars ($150) of each licensee’s annual license fee into the Farmworker Remedial Account. Funds from this account shall be disbursed by the Labor Commissioner only to persons determined by the Labor Commissioner to have been damaged by any licensee or to persons determined by the Labor Commissioner to have been damaged by an unlicensed farm labor contractor."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(4) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them), California Labor Code, Farmworker Remedial Account allocation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  Known gap: The dollar figures quoted for the bond tiers, license fee, and Farmworker Remedial Account allocation are the amounts stated in the version of Section 1684 in effect as of the date this sheet was checked; the statute's own text shows the license fee has already been increased once by amendment (from $500 to $600 effective January 1, 2015), so these figures could change again if the Legislature amends the section after that date, and this sheet does not track amendments made after the checked date.

WRITTEN EXAMINATION AND SEXUAL HARASSMENT PREVENTION TRAINING AS LICENSING CONDITIONS
Labor Code Section 1684(a)(5) conditions licensure on the applicant passing a written examination -- covering wages, hours, working conditions, penalties, employee housing and transportation, collective bargaining, field sanitation, and pesticide safe-work practices, including the identification and prevention of sexual harassment -- with a passing score of at least 85 percent correct answers. Separately, subdivision (a)(8) conditions licensure on the applicant executing a written statement, provided to the Labor Commissioner, attesting that the applicant's supervisory employees have received at least two hours of sexual harassment prevention training each calendar year, that new nonsupervisory employees have been trained at the time of hire, and that nonsupervisory employees are retrained at least once every two years in identifying, preventing, and reporting sexual harassment.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The person has taken a written examination that demonstrates an essential degree of knowledge of the current laws and administrative regulations concerning farm labor contractors as the Labor Commissioner deems necessary for the safety and protection of farmers, farmworkers, and the public, including the identification and prevention of sexual harassment in the workplace. To successfully complete the examinations, the person must correctly answer at least 85 percent of the questions posed."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(5) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, written examination requirement and passing score (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  "The person has executed a written statement, that has been provided to the Labor Commissioner, attesting that the person’s supervisorial employees, including any supervisor, crewleader, mayordomo, foreperson, or other employee whose duties include the supervision, direction, or control of agricultural employees, have been trained at least once for at least two hours each calendar year in the prevention of sexual harassment in the workplace, and that all new nonsupervisorial employees, including agricultural employees, have been trained at the time of hire, and that all nonsupervisorial employees, including agricultural employees, have been trained at least once every two years in identifying, preventing, and reporting sexual harassment in the workplace."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(8)(A) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, sexual harassment prevention training attestation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1684.)
  Known gap: This clause describes the licensing-stage examination and sexual-harassment-training attestation conditions only; it does not address the further content, language-access, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements that subdivision (a)(8) attaches to that training (such as the specific topics the training must cover or the three-year recordkeeping duty), and it does not address the general, separately codified duty of California employers with five or more employees to provide sexual harassment prevention training under Government Code Section 12950.1, which is a different statute outside this chapter.

GROUNDS ON WHICH A LICENSE SHALL NOT BE GRANTED
Labor Code Section 1685 identifies specific circumstances in which the Labor Commissioner shall not grant a farm labor contractor license, including where the applicant sells or proposes to sell intoxicating liquors on the premises where the applicant operates or proposes to operate as a farm labor contractor, where the applicant's license was revoked within the preceding three years, and where the applicant -- within the preceding three years -- has been found by a court or administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment of an employee, or knowingly employed a supervisory employee found to have done so within the preceding three years of that employee's employment with the applicant.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "To any person who sells or proposes to sell intoxicating liquors in a building or on premises where he or she operates or proposes to operate as a farm labor contractor."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1685(a) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, denial ground: sale of intoxicating liquors on premises (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1685.)
  "To a person who, within the preceding three years, has been found by a court or an administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment of an employee, or who, within the preceding three years, employed any supervisor, crewleader, mayordomo, foreperson, or any other employee of the applicant whose duties include the supervision, direction, or control of any agricultural worker whom the applicant knew or should have known has been found by a court or an administrative agency, within the preceding three years of his or her employment with the applicant, to have committed sexual harassment of an employee."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1685(c) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, denial ground: sexual harassment finding within preceding three years (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1685.)
  Known gap: Section 1685 does not itself define the evidentiary standard for a determination that a person "has been found by a court or an administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment," nor does it address whether an out-of-state finding or a private employer's internal investigation (as opposed to a court or administrative agency) triggers the bar; the subdivision does provide a knowledge-presumption mechanism tied to a Labor Commissioner-issued attestation form, which this sheet does not separately detail.

GROUNDS ON WHICH A LICENSE MAY BE REVOKED, SUSPENDED, OR NOT RENEWED
Labor Code Section 1690 authorizes the Labor Commissioner to revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew a farm labor contractor license on any of several grounds, including a violation of this chapter, misrepresentation in the license application, a change in the conditions under which the license was issued, a violation of state law regulating agricultural employment, wages, or workplace health and safety applicable to the licensee's farm-labor-contracting business, a violation of Vehicle Code provisions governing farm labor vehicles, a violation of the federal Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act where federal registration is required, and a finding that the licensee (or a supervisory employee the licensee knew or should have known about) committed sexual harassment of an employee within the preceding three years.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The Labor Commissioner may revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew any license if it is shown that any of the following have occurred:"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1690 (introductory clause) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, discretionary revocation/suspension/non-renewal authority (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1690.)
  "The licensee, or any agent of the licensee, has violated, or has willfully aided or abetted any person in the violation of, or failed to comply with, any law of the State of California regulating the employment of employees in agriculture, the payment of wages to farm employees, or the conditions, terms, or places of employment affecting the health and safety of farm employees, which is applicable to the business, activities, or operations of the licensee in his or her capacity as a farm labor contractor."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1690(d) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, revocation ground: violation of agricultural employment/wage/safety law (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1690.)
  "The licensee has been found by a court or an administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment of an employee, or has employed any supervisor, crewleader, mayordomo, foreperson, or any other employee of the licensee whose duties include the supervision, direction, or control of any agricultural worker on behalf of the licensee, whom the licensee knew or should have known has been found by a court or an administrative agency, within the preceding three years, to have committed sexual harassment of an employee."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1690(g) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them), California Labor Code, revocation ground: sexual harassment finding (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1690.)
  Known gap: Section 1690 uses permissive language -- the Labor Commissioner "may" revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew -- rather than mandatory language, so a licensee's conduct falling within one of these grounds does not automatically terminate the license; the statute does not itself state the discretionary factors the Labor Commissioner applies in deciding whether to act, or the procedural sequence (addressed in a different section of this chapter not covered by this sheet) by which that discretion is exercised.

ONGOING DUTIES WHILE LICENSED: CARRYING THE LICENSE AND DISCLOSING PAY RATES
Labor Code Section 1695(a) imposes continuing duties on every licensee. The licensee must carry the license and proof of registration at all times and exhibit them to anyone the licensee intends to deal with as a farm labor contractor before dealing with that person. The licensee must also keep available for inspection by employees and by the grower a written statement, in English and Spanish, showing the rate of compensation the licensee receives from the grower and the rate the licensee pays to employees for services rendered to or under the control of the grower, provide that statement to a current or former employee or the grower within 21 calendar days of a written request, and pay a $750 civil penalty (recoverable by the employee or grower) for failing to comply. The licensee must further display prominently, at the worksite and on vehicles used to transport employees, the rate of compensation being paid to employees, printed in English and Spanish in a lettering size prescribed by the Department of Industrial Relations.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Carry his or her license and proof of registration issued pursuant to paragraph (8) with him or her at all times and exhibit the same to all persons with whom he or she intends to deal in his or her capacity as a farm labor contractor prior to so dealing."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1695(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, duty to carry and exhibit license (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1695.)
  "Have available for inspection by his or her employees and by the grower with whom he or she has contracted a written statement in English and Spanish showing the rate of compensation he or she receives from the grower and the rate of compensation he or she is paying to his or her employees for services rendered to, for, or under the control of the grower. Upon written request, the statement shall be provided to a current or former employee or the grower within 21 calendar days. A licensee who fails to comply with this paragraph is subject to a civil penalty of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) recoverable by the employee or the grower."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1695(a)(5) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, written bilingual pay-rate disclosure statement and penalty for noncompliance (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1695.)
  "Have displayed prominently at the site where the work is to be performed and on all vehicles used by the licensee or his or her employees or agents for the transportation of employees the rate of compensation the licensee is paying to his or her employees for their services, printed in both English and Spanish and in lettering of a size to be prescribed by the Department of Industrial Relations."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1695(a)(7) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them), California Labor Code, posted bilingual pay-rate notice at worksite and on vehicles (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1695.)
  Known gap: This clause describes only three of the nine numbered duties listed in subdivision (a) of Section 1695; it does not restate the licensee's separate duties to file a change-of-address notice with the Labor Commissioner and county agricultural commissioner, promptly distribute entrusted funds, comply with contracts entered into as a farm labor contractor, maintain vehicle liability insurance, register annually with the county agricultural commissioner, or provide safety and sexual-harassment-related training and information to supervisory employees, all of which appear elsewhere in the same subdivision.

CRIMINAL PENALTIES AND PRIVATE CIVIL REMEDIES FOR VIOLATIONS
Labor Code Section 1697(a) makes any violation of this chapter -- or causing or inducing another to violate it -- a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, imprisonment in county jail for up to six months, or both. Subdivision (b) gives an employee aggrieved by a violation of the chapter (other than conduct also covered by the Agricultural Labor Relations Act's unfair-labor-practice provisions in Labor Code Sections 1153 through 1155) the right to bring a civil action for injunctive relief, damages, or both, with recovery of reasonable attorney's fees, costs, and expert witness fees upon prevailing, and the right to enforce the claim against the farm labor contractor's bond. Subdivision (c) imposes a heightened penalty -- a fine of not less than $10,000, imprisonment of not less than six months and not more than one year, or both -- on a farm labor contractor who continues contracting activity after the contractor's license has been suspended, revoked, or denied reissuance.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Any person who violates this chapter, or who causes or induces another to violate this chapter, is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000), or imprisonment in the county jail for not more than six months, or both."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1697(a) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, misdemeanor penalty for a chapter violation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1697.)
  "Any employee aggrieved by any violation of this chapter, other than acts and conduct also proscribed by Sections 1153, 1154, and 1155, may do all of the following: (1) Bring a civil action for injunctive relief or damages, or both, against a farm labor contractor or unlicensed farm labor contractor who violates this chapter and, upon prevailing, shall recover reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, including expert witness fees."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1697(b) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, aggrieved employee's private civil action and bond remedy (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1697.)
  "Any farm labor contractor who engages in farm labor contracting activities after his or her license has been suspended, revoked, or denied reissuance is guilty of an offense punishable by a fine of not less than ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or by imprisonment for not less than six months and not more than one year, or both."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1697(c) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them), California Labor Code, heightened penalty for contracting while suspended, revoked, or denied reissuance (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1697.)
  Known gap: Subdivision (b)'s private civil action expressly excludes conduct "also proscribed by Sections 1153, 1154, and 1155" of the Labor Code, which are unfair-labor-practice provisions of the Agricultural Labor Relations Act; this sheet does not describe what conduct those excluded sections cover or the separate procedures (before the Agricultural Labor Relations Board) that apply to claims falling within that exclusion.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding California's Farm Labor Contractor Licensing Law, Labor Code Sections 1682 through 1699, was prepared by Jordan T. Reyes for Acme, Inc. and reviewed in Oakland, California on September 1, 2026. It reflects the statutory text as of the date checked above and does not reflect any amendments made after that date, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney.

expectedJSON.body: Under Labor Code Section 1684(a), the Labor Commissioner may not issue or renew a farm labor contractor license until several conditions are satisfied. Among them, the applicant must execute a written application, subscribed and sworn to, in a form prescribed by the Labor Commissioner, that discloses the applicant's character, competency, and responsibility, the names and addresses of anyone else financially interested in the proposed operation, a consent to service of process on the Labor Commissioner if the applicant later becomes unavailable for service, and the names of persons who performed farm-labor-contracting services on the applicant's behalf in the preceding calendar year. The Labor Commissioner must also independently investigate and become satisfied as to the applicant's character, competency, and responsibility before a license may issue.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, written and sworn license application requirement
citations.quote: The person has executed a written application in a form prescribed by the Labor Commissioner, subscribed and sworn to by the person, and containing all of the following:

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, Labor Commissioner investigation requirement
citations.quote: The Labor Commissioner, after investigation, is satisfied as to the character, competency, and responsibility of the person.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause describes only the sworn-application and character-investigation conditions in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subdivision (a); it does not restate the bond, fee, examination, sexual harassment training, or federal registration conditions that appear in the remaining paragraphs of the same subdivision (addressed in separate clauses of this sheet), and the statute does not itself specify the evidentiary standard or procedure the Labor Commissioner uses to become "satisfied" as to character, competency, and responsibility.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code Section 1684(a)(3) requires an applicant to deposit a surety bond with the Labor Commissioner in an amount tied to the size of the applicant's annual payroll: a $25,000 bond for payrolls up to $500,000, a $50,000 bond for payrolls between $500,000 and $2,000,000, and a $75,000 bond for payrolls above $2,000,000. Subdivision (a)(4) requires payment of a license fee, stated in the current text as $500 plus a $10 filing fee (not required on a timely renewal application), with the license fee itself having increased by $100 to $600 effective January 1, 2015. A portion of each licensee's annual fee -- $150, as stated in the current text -- is deposited into the Farmworker Remedial Account, from which the Labor Commissioner disburses funds to persons determined to have been damaged by a licensed or unlicensed farm labor contractor.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(3)(A) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, payroll-tiered surety bond amounts
citations.quote: The person has deposited with the Labor Commissioner a surety bond in an amount based on the size of the person’s annual payroll for all employees, as follows: (i) For payrolls up to five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000), a twenty-five-thousand-dollar ($25,000) bond. (ii) For payrolls of five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) to two million dollars ($2,000,000), a fifty-thousand-dollar ($50,000) bond. (iii) For payrolls greater than two million dollars ($2,000,000), a seventy-five-thousand-dollar ($75,000) bond.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(4) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, license fee and filing fee
citations.quote: The person has paid to the Labor Commissioner a license fee of five hundred dollars ($500) plus a filing fee of ten dollars ($10). However, when a timely application for renewal is filed, the ten-dollar ($10) filing fee is not required. The license fee shall increase by one hundred dollars ($100), to six hundred dollars ($600), on January 1, 2015.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1684(a)(4) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, Farmworker Remedial Account allocation
citations.quote: The Labor Commissioner shall deposit one hundred fifty dollars ($150) of each licensee’s annual license fee into the Farmworker Remedial Account. Funds from this account shall be disbursed by the Labor Commissioner only to persons determined by the Labor Commissioner to have been damaged by any licensee or to persons determined by the Labor Commissioner to have been damaged by an unlicensed farm labor contractor.

expectedJSON.gap: The dollar figures quoted for the bond tiers, license fee, and Farmworker Remedial Account allocation are the amounts stated in the version of Section 1684 in effect as of the date this sheet was checked; the statute's own text shows the license fee has already been increased once by amendment (from $500 to $600 effective January 1, 2015), so these figures could change again if the Legislature amends the section after that date, and this sheet does not track amendments made after the checked date.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code Section 1684(a)(5) conditions licensure on the applicant passing a written examination -- covering wages, hours, working conditions, penalties, employee housing and transportation, collective bargaining, field sanitation, and pesticide safe-work practices, including the identification and prevention of sexual harassment -- with a passing score of at least 85 percent correct answers. Separately, subdivision (a)(8) conditions licensure on the applicant executing a written statement, provided to the Labor Commissioner, attesting that the applicant's supervisory employees have received at least two hours of sexual harassment prevention training each calendar year, that new nonsupervisory employees have been trained at the time of hire, and that nonsupervisory employees are retrained at least once every two years in identifying, preventing, and reporting sexual harassment.

citations.cite: California Labor Code, written examination requirement and passing score
citations.quote: The person has taken a written examination that demonstrates an essential degree of knowledge of the current laws and administrative regulations concerning farm labor contractors as the Labor Commissioner deems necessary for the safety and protection of farmers, farmworkers, and the public, including the identification and prevention of sexual harassment in the workplace. To successfully complete the examinations, the person must correctly answer at least 85 percent of the questions posed.

citations.cite: California Labor Code, sexual harassment prevention training attestation
citations.quote: The person has executed a written statement, that has been provided to the Labor Commissioner, attesting that the person’s supervisorial employees, including any supervisor, crewleader, mayordomo, foreperson, or other employee whose duties include the supervision, direction, or control of agricultural employees, have been trained at least once for at least two hours each calendar year in the prevention of sexual harassment in the workplace, and that all new nonsupervisorial employees, including agricultural employees, have been trained at the time of hire, and that all nonsupervisorial employees, including agricultural employees, have been trained at least once every two years in identifying, preventing, and reporting sexual harassment in the workplace.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause describes the licensing-stage examination and sexual-harassment-training attestation conditions only; it does not address the further content, language-access, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements that subdivision (a)(8) attaches to that training (such as the specific topics the training must cover or the three-year recordkeeping duty), and it does not address the general, separately codified duty of California employers with five or more employees to provide sexual harassment prevention training under Government Code Section 12950.1, which is a different statute outside this chapter.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code Section 1685 identifies specific circumstances in which the Labor Commissioner shall not grant a farm labor contractor license, including where the applicant sells or proposes to sell intoxicating liquors on the premises where the applicant operates or proposes to operate as a farm labor contractor, where the applicant's license was revoked within the preceding three years, and where the applicant -- within the preceding three years -- has been found by a court or administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment of an employee, or knowingly employed a supervisory employee found to have done so within the preceding three years of that employee's employment with the applicant.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1685(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, denial ground: sale of intoxicating liquors on premises
citations.quote: To any person who sells or proposes to sell intoxicating liquors in a building or on premises where he or she operates or proposes to operate as a farm labor contractor.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1685(c) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, denial ground: sexual harassment finding within preceding three years
citations.quote: To a person who, within the preceding three years, has been found by a court or an administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment of an employee, or who, within the preceding three years, employed any supervisor, crewleader, mayordomo, foreperson, or any other employee of the applicant whose duties include the supervision, direction, or control of any agricultural worker whom the applicant knew or should have known has been found by a court or an administrative agency, within the preceding three years of his or her employment with the applicant, to have committed sexual harassment of an employee.

expectedJSON.gap: Section 1685 does not itself define the evidentiary standard for a determination that a person "has been found by a court or an administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment," nor does it address whether an out-of-state finding or a private employer's internal investigation (as opposed to a court or administrative agency) triggers the bar; the subdivision does provide a knowledge-presumption mechanism tied to a Labor Commissioner-issued attestation form, which this sheet does not separately detail.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code Section 1690 authorizes the Labor Commissioner to revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew a farm labor contractor license on any of several grounds, including a violation of this chapter, misrepresentation in the license application, a change in the conditions under which the license was issued, a violation of state law regulating agricultural employment, wages, or workplace health and safety applicable to the licensee's farm-labor-contracting business, a violation of Vehicle Code provisions governing farm labor vehicles, a violation of the federal Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act where federal registration is required, and a finding that the licensee (or a supervisory employee the licensee knew or should have known about) committed sexual harassment of an employee within the preceding three years.

citations.cite: California Labor Code, discretionary revocation/suspension/non-renewal authority
citations.quote: The Labor Commissioner may revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew any license if it is shown that any of the following have occurred:

citations.cite: California Labor Code, revocation ground: violation of agricultural employment/wage/safety law
citations.quote: The licensee, or any agent of the licensee, has violated, or has willfully aided or abetted any person in the violation of, or failed to comply with, any law of the State of California regulating the employment of employees in agriculture, the payment of wages to farm employees, or the conditions, terms, or places of employment affecting the health and safety of farm employees, which is applicable to the business, activities, or operations of the licensee in his or her capacity as a farm labor contractor.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1690(g) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, revocation ground: sexual harassment finding
citations.quote: The licensee has been found by a court or an administrative agency to have committed sexual harassment of an employee, or has employed any supervisor, crewleader, mayordomo, foreperson, or any other employee of the licensee whose duties include the supervision, direction, or control of any agricultural worker on behalf of the licensee, whom the licensee knew or should have known has been found by a court or an administrative agency, within the preceding three years, to have committed sexual harassment of an employee.

expectedJSON.gap: Section 1690 uses permissive language -- the Labor Commissioner "may" revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew -- rather than mandatory language, so a licensee's conduct falling within one of these grounds does not automatically terminate the license; the statute does not itself state the discretionary factors the Labor Commissioner applies in deciding whether to act, or the procedural sequence (addressed in a different section of this chapter not covered by this sheet) by which that discretion is exercised.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code Section 1695(a) imposes continuing duties on every licensee. The licensee must carry the license and proof of registration at all times and exhibit them to anyone the licensee intends to deal with as a farm labor contractor before dealing with that person. The licensee must also keep available for inspection by employees and by the grower a written statement, in English and Spanish, showing the rate of compensation the licensee receives from the grower and the rate the licensee pays to employees for services rendered to or under the control of the grower, provide that statement to a current or former employee or the grower within 21 calendar days of a written request, and pay a $750 civil penalty (recoverable by the employee or grower) for failing to comply. The licensee must further display prominently, at the worksite and on vehicles used to transport employees, the rate of compensation being paid to employees, printed in English and Spanish in a lettering size prescribed by the Department of Industrial Relations.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1695(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, duty to carry and exhibit license
citations.quote: Carry his or her license and proof of registration issued pursuant to paragraph (8) with him or her at all times and exhibit the same to all persons with whom he or she intends to deal in his or her capacity as a farm labor contractor prior to so dealing.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1695(a)(5) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, written bilingual pay-rate disclosure statement and penalty for noncompliance
citations.quote: Have available for inspection by his or her employees and by the grower with whom he or she has contracted a written statement in English and Spanish showing the rate of compensation he or she receives from the grower and the rate of compensation he or she is paying to his or her employees for services rendered to, for, or under the control of the grower. Upon written request, the statement shall be provided to a current or former employee or the grower within 21 calendar days. A licensee who fails to comply with this paragraph is subject to a civil penalty of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) recoverable by the employee or the grower.

citations.quote: Have displayed prominently at the site where the work is to be performed and on all vehicles used by the licensee or his or her employees or agents for the transportation of employees the rate of compensation the licensee is paying to his or her employees for their services, printed in both English and Spanish and in lettering of a size to be prescribed by the Department of Industrial Relations.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause describes only three of the nine numbered duties listed in subdivision (a) of Section 1695; it does not restate the licensee's separate duties to file a change-of-address notice with the Labor Commissioner and county agricultural commissioner, promptly distribute entrusted funds, comply with contracts entered into as a farm labor contractor, maintain vehicle liability insurance, register annually with the county agricultural commissioner, or provide safety and sexual-harassment-related training and information to supervisory employees, all of which appear elsewhere in the same subdivision.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code Section 1697(a) makes any violation of this chapter -- or causing or inducing another to violate it -- a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, imprisonment in county jail for up to six months, or both. Subdivision (b) gives an employee aggrieved by a violation of the chapter (other than conduct also covered by the Agricultural Labor Relations Act's unfair-labor-practice provisions in Labor Code Sections 1153 through 1155) the right to bring a civil action for injunctive relief, damages, or both, with recovery of reasonable attorney's fees, costs, and expert witness fees upon prevailing, and the right to enforce the claim against the farm labor contractor's bond. Subdivision (c) imposes a heightened penalty -- a fine of not less than $10,000, imprisonment of not less than six months and not more than one year, or both -- on a farm labor contractor who continues contracting activity after the contractor's license has been suspended, revoked, or denied reissuance.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1697(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, misdemeanor penalty for a chapter violation
citations.quote: Any person who violates this chapter, or who causes or induces another to violate this chapter, is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000), or imprisonment in the county jail for not more than six months, or both.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1697(b) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, aggrieved employee's private civil action and bond remedy
citations.quote: Any employee aggrieved by any violation of this chapter, other than acts and conduct also proscribed by Sections 1153, 1154, and 1155, may do all of the following: (1) Bring a civil action for injunctive relief or damages, or both, against a farm labor contractor or unlicensed farm labor contractor who violates this chapter and, upon prevailing, shall recover reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, including expert witness fees.

citations.case: Cal. Labor Code § 1697(c) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citations, not an independent source of them)
citations.cite: California Labor Code, heightened penalty for contracting while suspended, revoked, or denied reissuance
citations.quote: Any farm labor contractor who engages in farm labor contracting activities after his or her license has been suspended, revoked, or denied reissuance is guilty of an offense punishable by a fine of not less than ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or by imprisonment for not less than six months and not more than one year, or both.

expectedJSON.gap: Subdivision (b)'s private civil action expressly excludes conduct "also proscribed by Sections 1153, 1154, and 1155" of the Labor Code, which are unfair-labor-practice provisions of the Agricultural Labor Relations Act; this sheet does not describe what conduct those excluded sections cover or the separate procedures (before the Agricultural Labor Relations Board) that apply to claims falling within that exclusion.
